nodes.title: Counterposition: the arbitrage layer entrenches rentiers
nodes.description: The joker’s brief against the microenterprise layer.
nodes.body:
# Counterposition: the arbitrage layer entrenches rentiers

**The joker writes:** An information-arbitrage layer that owns neither need nor supply still extracts rent from both. You have invented a middleman and called it a commons. Show me why this does not become the very rentier structure you set out to dissolve.

nodes.title: Build societal capability to respond
nodes.parent: Reduce climate mortality and its politics
nodes.description: The deepest layer of the nest: can a society respond at all?
nodes.body:
# Build societal capability to respond

The deepest cut. Beneath mortality-and-politics is the question of whether a society has the *capability* to respond at all. Solve here and the layers above move.

Rests on [[Response capability is buildable]] and [[Information arbitrage can be enterprised]].

nodes.title: Reduce climate mortality and its politics
nodes.description: Under water deprivation: who dies, and the politics of that.
nodes.body:
# Reduce climate mortality and its politics

nodes.title: Hold warming to 1.5°C
nodes.description: The surface framing everyone reaches for first — a temperature target.
nodes.body:
# Hold warming to 1.5°C

The obvious goal. But a temperature target is a *cut* through a deeper, nested problem space. Descend to see what actually sits underneath it.

This rests on [[Anticipatory action beats reactive relief]].

nodes.title: Prevent mass water deprivation
nodes.description: Under the temperature target sits the lived harm: water.
nodes.body:
# Prevent mass water deprivation

Beneath the 1.5° framing, the harm people actually meet is water deprivation. Solving for temperature is not the same as solving for this.

Rests on [[Optionality is substitutable capital]].

nodes.title: Outcomes capital pool

# Outcomes capital pool

Feeds the accelerator. Releases against realised outcomes.

nodes.title: Outcome accelerator
nodes.description: A dynamic matching function between a constructed demand space and a supply space, funded against outcomes.
nodes.body:
# Outcome accelerator

Not a procurement desk. A *matching function*: it continuously pairs constructed demand with available supply and settles against outcomes.

## Ontological shift
From buying outputs to matching for outcomes.

## What it means
Demand is constructed, not assumed; supply is discovered, not pre-listed; capital follows realised outcomes.

## Plausibility pathway
Start with one bioregion, one water-deprivation demand space, three supply archetypes.

## Communication
“You don’t buy the outcome. You fund the matching that produces it.”

nodes.title: Fixed procurement (counter-model)
nodes.description: The incumbent model shown for contrast: cost it, buy it, pre-purchase the output.
nodes.body:
# Fixed procurement

The counter-model. You specify the output, cost it, and buy it up front. No matching, no discovery, no outcome settlement.

nodes.title: Optionality as infrastructure
nodes.description: Reframing preserved future options as a kind of public infrastructure.
nodes.body:
# Optionality as infrastructure

## Ontological shift
From optionality as a private hedge to optionality as shared infrastructure.

## What it means
Indicators: number of preserved reversible pathways per system.

## Plausibility pathway
Pilot in one bioregion’s water system.

## Communication
“Keep the doors open, together.”

nodes.title: Week 26 — nesting the water goal changed the portfolio
nodes.description: Descending from temperature to water reshuffled which portfolio items mattered.
nodes.body:
## Deviation
Re-cutting the goal from temperature to water deprivation moved three portfolio items up and two down.

## Wider-world connection
The temperature framing dominates funding calls; the water framing dominates lived harm.

## Early signals
Partners engage faster with the water cut.

## Counterposition
Don’t abandon the temperature framing — hold both cuts visible at once.

nodes.title: Week 27 — the accelerator wanted to become a procurement desk
nodes.description: This week the model drifted back toward pre-purchasing outputs.
nodes.body:
## Deviation
The accelerator design kept collapsing into a procurement desk — pre-specifying and buying outputs.

## Wider-world connection
Mirrors how outcome funds in the wild quietly revert to output contracts under audit pressure.

## Early signals
Two partners asked for a fixed price list in week 26.

## Counterposition
Hold the matching function open; refuse the price list; price the *match*, not the output.
